### Us fed laUnches Qe3; ecb and china initiate stimUlUs measUres...is it enoUgh? last month, we had highlighted the sluggish growth in the Bric economies, as well as in the more mature ones, and asked if more Qe was needed. While we thought it was, in order to stimulate sentiment and hopefully demand, the timing of any measures was uncertain, and prices in general were languishing as a result. however, the united States’ Federal reserve took action this month and base metals enjoyed a sharp rally following this and other recent stimulus measures. The lme index has rallied 10% since the end of august on expectation for, and then delivery of, action on monetary policy. The index did, however, ease around 2% from its recent high as the initial market euphoria has been tempered. only the uS Fed implemented “full” quantitative easing, while the ecB and china have so far stopped short. The euro rallied against the dollar, and risky assets (including metals) started to climb, following the european central Bank’s launch of a new and open-ended sovereign bond-buying programme on September 6th. The focus of the scheme would be on bonds maturing within three years and only applies to countries that agree to strict policy conditions. The ecB President said that “no exante quantitative limits are set on the size of outright monet

ary transactions”. in a concession to concerns by private investors as to their place in the queue in the event of a sovereign default (and thus enhance confidence and stimulate investment), the ecB would waive its senior credit status on purchased bonds. The ecB’s move was swiftly followed by china, which also stopped short of full-blown quantitative easing. The National Development and reform commission announced approvals for around 60 infrastructure projects worth around $157 billion, including highways, ports and airport runways. china has continued to be plagued by weak economic conditions, and recent data releases have done nothing to suggest a looming turnaround. analysts have been steadily revising lower their forecasts for economic growth and are now closer in line with the chinese government’s forecast for 7.5% GDP growth for this year; Thomson reuters GFmS is currently projecting annual growth this year and next at 7.7% and 7.9%, respectively. it should be noted, however, that china’s recent infrastructure spending plan represents only around one quarter of the 4 trillion yuan ($630 million) stimulus programme launched in 2008/2009. These previous two central bank actions had primed the market for more, and risky asset prices and market positioning were starting to reflect this. The Fed didn’t disappoint, announcing a fairly aggressive programme on September 13th, pledging to buy $40 billion of mortgage-backed securities (mBS) every month until it saw a sustained upturn in the weak jobs market. By focusing on mBS, the Fed hopes to push mortgage rates lower, stimulating the depressed housing market, and also encourage investors to switch out of these products into other assets, such as corporate bonds, lowering yields there as well. additionally, the Fed said that it was unlikely to raise overnight interest rates until at least mid-2015 (compared to late-2014 previously) and that it would pursue an easy monetary policy “for a considerable time” even after the economy strengthened. The openended nature of this plan, coupled with the extension of any possible rate increase, could in theory mean a massive injection of liquidity over a period of time if unemployment doesn’t recover sufficiently to achieve the Fed’s (unreleased) target. ###### BaSe meTalS & oTher commoDiTy PriceS ###### BaSe meTal PriceS iN major curreNcieS 300

### ALUMINIUM ###### recent developments ###### outlook for the next twelve months **•** **_Along with the rest of the base metals complex, aluminium prices received a boost from the recent QE3 announcement by the Federal Reserve, with the LME cash price hitting a recent high of $2,200/tonne. However, markets have subsequently eased lower, and aluminium was trading around $2,125/tonne at the time of writing._** **•** **_The level of reported inventories has continued its recent trend upwards. LME stocks are now only just short of their all-time high of 5.126 million tonnes, while Shanghai exchange, Japanese port and IAI unwrought stocks have all been rising too. Combined reported inventories now stand 2.7% higher than at the start of the year._** **•** **_The market has failed so far, especially in China, to manage production in line with weakening demand and burgeoning stocks. As we have noted here and previously, a number of smelters globally continue to be thrown (potential) lifelines, especially in terms of improved or subsidised power deals. Rusal has, though, recently announced some production curtailments from late-2012 through 2018, but these amount to only 275,000 tpy._** **•** **_We will be revisiting our annual forecasts for 2012 and 2013 in next month’s report. Currently we are projecting a surplus of 416,000 tonnes for this year and an average cash price of $1,995/tonne._** **•** **_The lock-up of inventory in LME warehouses (with offtake queues potentially extending into June 2013) has kept the upward pressure on physical premiums. Whilst there has not been the same magnitude of rises seen a few months ago, the creep higher continues. European duty-paid quotes are $5-10/tonne higher than last month, at $270-280/tonne. Japanese spot premiums are unchanged at $250/tonne, but indications for Q4 term premiums are $255-258/tonne. US Midwest quotes are up around 0.5¢/lb to 11-11.5¢/lb._** **•** **_Global demand is estimated by the WBMS to have risen by 4.0% during the first half of 2012. ###### market background the recent round of quantitative easing by the federal reserve, combined with stimulus measures (which fell short of full-blown Qe) from china and the ecb, prompted a rally across risky assets, including industrial commodities. this was, though, basically an extra fillip to an aluminium market that had been on an upward trend since hitting its annual low of $1,827/tonne on august 16th. the cash price rallied to a recent high of $2,200/tonne, but post-fed market euphoria started to fray and the broader market softening has seen aluminium prices trading around $2,125 at the time of writing. we had noted previously that aluminium prices had been pushing further below their marginal costs, and that this would limit the metal’s downside risk. ongoing stock financing, with lme inventories returning close to their all-time high, also continues to provide underlying support to prices and a continued boost to physical premiums. nevertheless, production curtailments necessary to address the market surplus situation have not been forthcoming, and last month’s slip in reported chinese production proved to be only an aberration. ###### total reported inventories up 2.7% up for year-to-date as stocks continue to build combining all reported stocks now takes the year-todate total to 7.024 million tonnes, 2.7% higher than the end-2011 number. lme stocks have been on an upward trajectory since June. although they added only 6,525 tonnes in august, they have been bolstered by a further 132,775 tonnes since then, to once again breach 5 million tonnes (5.018), only slightly short of the record of 5.126 million tonnes. cancelled warrants as a ratio of the total have slipped to almost 31%, perhaps indicating that more metal is finding its long-term financing home. however, potential lead times for offtake, at vlissingen in particular, have lengthened, pushing into June 2013. for the year- week

mine production and refined production continue to exhibit divergent trends 

as noted in previous reports, along with the weakness in the global demand environment, the strength of global mine production has been a key factor behind our cautious outlook on the zinc market.  on a global basis, output expanded by 10.9% over the opening six months of the year, according to the latest ilzsG statistics.  key areas of growth were china (+567,000 tonnes) and mexico (+35,000 tonnes), which outweighed declines in peru (-23,000 tonnes) and the united states (-16,000 tonnes). despite the decline in zinc prices over the third quarter, many zinc operations remained profitable and, as such (and given our forecasts for higher prices over the close of the year), we expect that global mine production will continue to record strong growth going forward. 

meanwhile, in contrast, smelters are being impacted by weakening demand and low treatment charges.  Global refined output fell 1.1% over the January-June period, driven by a 7.3% fall in chinese output, in addition to declines in Brazil (-17,000 tonnes) and south africa (-41,000 tonnes). such weakness was only partly offset by growth in india (+36,000 tonnes), Japan (+63,000 tonnes) and south korea (+31,000 tonnes).
